newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, but off highs.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen contract on TIFFE ended Friday's day session firmer but off its highs after giving up some early gains.

The contract eased back after Takayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's research and statistics department, said that there were times in the past when there was a discrepancy between the real economy and the financial markets' views of the economy.

The market took his remark as an indirect warning over recent euphoria in the debt market stemming from a strong market belief that the central bank will not tighten credit before mid-1997, traders said.
Matsushima added that the BOJ has not changed its view that the economy is continuing to grow gradually, but is generally more optimistic following the recent release of economic data.

Earlier, the September rose to a high of 99.33, but gains were partly slashed by a lack of outright JGB purchases by the Ministry of Finance's Trust Fund Bureau which had been expected by the market, traders said.
The December jumped to a high of 99.24 from 99.16 on Thursday, helped by traders' stop-loss buying at 99.21-22.
Despite some recovery in the key Nikkei 225 share average, shares in the banking and brokerage sectors remained weak.

"As long as bank shares stay bearish, bargain-hunting emerges on dips and protects the downside (of Euroyen prices) But the market has been wary of any official warning, even a subtle one, against steep gains," said a bank trader.
In the Euro interbank market, the Japan premium -- the extra cost Japanese banks are charged when raising funds -- fell slightly, but is still at high levels.
Major Japanese city banks were paying premiums of about 31 basis points over the prevailing one-month Eurodollar deposit rate of 5.59375 percent.

Traders said some local banks with funding difficulties were raising yen funds in the local interbank market and converting them into dollars in the currency forward market to meet their dollar needs.
The key overnight call rate was at 0.48 percent, down from the weighted average of 0.50 percent on Thursday.
The TIFFE is closed on Monday for a Japanese national holiday.---Yoshiko Mori, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8676
